text:
incident-bot: Pager: reserved-pool eu-central-1-resv-7 at 07:02 UTC — queue=1620, avg_wait=410s, throttles=119, affected=[AsteriaHealth, DeltaLedger]
oncall-sre: ack. moving to bridge. who can summarize?
marta: alerts around 07:01, autoscaler attempted several scales but kept failing with "quota_exceeded" and we are seeing a runaway from DeltaLedger long-running streaming sessions.
alex: grabbing logs. early note: eviction logic is evicting wrong priority classes under pressure (preemptible > reserved). patch incoming.
paul: customer impact? lia?
lia: AsteriaHealth endpoints returning 502/503s intermittently; DeltaLedger latency high but not total failure. Asteria on reserved GPUs.
oncall-sre: set mitigation priority to Asteria first. options: tenant shaping, evict preemptible batch, route warm traffic to fallback pool.
paul: contacting cloud quota team now. ETA unknown. applying immediate tenant shaping for DeltaLedger: concurrency_limit=30 (was 200).
ops-bot: Applied concurrency_limit for tenant=DeltaLedger by paul at 07:08 UTC :white_check_mark:
alex: autoscaler error snippet:
```
2026-03-14T07:04:58Z ERROR autoscaler: launch failed: QuotaError(region=eu-central-1, allowed=0)
2026-03-14T07:05:03Z WARN eviction: comparator returned unexpected order: preemptible high-priority
2026-03-14T07:05:10Z INFO routing: no fallback route for tenant=AsteriaHealth
```
marta: so two problems: quota gating + eviction comparator bug + missing fallback for Asteria. we need quick wins.
paul: quick wins: 1) pause batch workers in pool (non-customer-critical) 2) fix eviction comparator on canary and restart service 3) carve out routing for Asteria -> us-west-2-burst (we have capacity there)
lia: doing pause now.

ops-bot: kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/batch-workers-eu-central-1 --namespace=dedicated-resv :gear:

marta: queue dropped 1620 -> 980 after pausing batch. partial relief.
alex: deployed comparator fix to canary and restarted eviction-manager. note: need careful rollout to avoid premature evictions.
ops-bot: eviction-manager restart on pool eu-central-1-resv-7 (canary nodes) :repeat:

paul: cloud quota responded: provision request submitted, they can lift +4 GPUs in 28m. not immediate.
lia: routing change applied: split AsteriaHealth traffic 30%->us-west-2-burst. CSM notified.
alex: eviction-manager reclaimed 8 GPUs by evicting low-priority preemptibles. reclaimed_gpus=8 evicted_jobs=71
ops-bot: Eviction summary posted at 07:23 UTC :bar_chart:

marta: Asteria reports reduced 503s, but still seeing higher p99 latency on large inference jobs.
paul: enabling emergency autoscaler override to allow up to +2 instances if quota becomes available automatically. logged in runbook.
ops-bot: emergency-autoscaler-override enabled by paul at 07:26 UTC :bangbang:

lia: schedule: we need to follow up with DeltaLedger for noisy tenant mitigation and ask for job reconfiguration.
alex: opening a PR with comparator unit tests and metric eviction_reorder_count. will link in postmortem.
marta: initiating postmortem, Sev2 (enterprise reserved impacted). initial notes: root cause = quota gating + eviction-priority bug + missing tenant fallback. mitigations: tenant shaping, batch pause, eviction fix, cross-region routing, emergency quota request.
paul: recommend: pre-authorize emergency quota pool for reserved-capacity, add runbook steps to ensure fallback routes exist for enterprise tenants, add tenant-level circuit breakers.
lia: CSM to request RCA from us. I'll draft comms and propose post-incident call with AsteriaHealth.

oncall-sre: actions:
- keep DeltaLedger cap until queue <150 (owner: paul)
- monitor eviction_manager metrics for reorder spikes (owner: alex)
- finalize fallback routing as durable config (owner: lia)
- complete postmortem + runbook updates (owner: marta)

ops-bot: Queue timeline: 1620 -> 980 -> 420 -> 160 (stabilizing)
oncall-sre: moving to monitoring-only. will keep pager open for 45m.
ops-bot: Incident thread set to monitoring-only by oncall-sre at 07:47 UTC :white_check_mark:

participants: incident-bot, oncall-sre, marta, alex, paul, lia, ops-bot
